title: THE MYSTERY OF A HARDENED HEART

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But Sihon king of Heshbon refused to let us pass through. For the Lord your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate in order to give him into your hands, as he has now done. The Lord said to me, "See, I have begun to deliver Sihon and his country over to you. Now begin to conquer and possess his land." - Deut 2:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Sihon refused Israel's offer of peace, and Scripture tells us something mysterious and weighty: "the Lord your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate." This is a difficult truth, and we should handle it honestly rather than explaining it away. Somehow, in the outworking of God's justice and sovereign purpose, Sihon's own stubbornness served God's plan to give the land to Israel. God was not the author of Sihon's evil, but He sovereignly used even a hardened heart to accomplish His righteous ends.

We must hold this carefully. Scripture consistently teaches that people are responsible for their own choices; Sihon chose war and refused peace of his own will. Yet Scripture also teaches that God is sovereign over all, even over the hardened hearts of those who oppose Him. These truths sit together in ways our minds cannot fully unravel. Rather than forcing a neat explanation, we bow before a God whose wisdom and justice are higher than ours (Rom 11:33).

This should stir a holy reverence in us. God is not a force we can manipulate or a plan we can derail. Even the opposition of proud and stubborn people cannot thwart His purposes; He weaves even resistance into His sovereign design. Pharaoh's hardened heart, and here Sihon's, both ultimately served God's larger plan of deliverance for His people.

For us, there is both warning and comfort. The warning: let us not harden our hearts against God, but respond to Him with soft, trusting hearts (Heb 3:15). The comfort: no opposition, however fierce, can defeat God's purposes for His people. The same sovereign God who used Sihon's stubbornness works all things according to His will, and in Christ He has secured our final victory. Trust the God whose purposes cannot fail.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you respond to truths about God that are hard to fully understand?
2. Are you keeping your own heart soft and responsive to God?
3. How does God's unstoppable sovereignty bring you comfort?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign God, Your wisdom and ways are far higher than mine. Keep my heart soft and responsive to You, and help me trust that no opposition can defeat Your purposes, which are secured for me in Christ. Amen.
